test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 72°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 56°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **right-angled ΔBDC**, ∠C = 90° − ∠DBC = 90° − 72° = 18°.

In **ΔAEC**, ∠AEB is the **exterior angle** at vertex E.

By the **Exterior Angle Theorem**, the exterior angle is the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

∴ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠ACE = 56° + 18° = 74°.

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In ΔABC, BD ⊥ AC at D, ∠DBC = 72°, and ∠CAE = 56°.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°; Linear pair of angles = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93980aeb0bc0ac433b49b2d628802ec05d1f4feea829273a0f32b79800268dd6.png] 

⇒ In **ΔBDC**, ∠BDC = 90° (since BD ⊥ AC).

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − (∠BDC + ∠DBC)

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − (90° + 72°) = 18°.

⇒ In **ΔAEC**, ∠CAE = 56° and ∠ACE = ∠BCD = 18°.

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − (∠CAE + ∠ACE)

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − (56° + 18°) = 106°.

⇒ Since B, E, and C lie on the same line, ∠AEB and ∠AEC form a **linear pair**.

⇒ ∠AEB = 180° − ∠AEC = 180° − 106° = 74°.

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Right-Angled Triangle

In a right-angled triangle, the two acute angles are complementary, meaning their sum is exactly 90°.</p
